claims.statement: China's geopolitical risk index reached a historic peak in March 2026, with 1.70% of newspaper articles covering China-related geopolitical risks, the highest level in the 10-year recent data series.
China's geopolitical risk remained elevated through May 2026 at 1.73% of articles, sustaining levels more than double the 2019-2021 average of approximately 0.7-0.8%.
As of October 2026, China's geopolitical risk index stood at 0.84% of articles, declining from the spring 2026 peak but remaining above the 2020-2021 baseline of 0.6-0.7%.
China experienced a sharp escalation in geopolitical risk from January to March 2026, with the index surging from 1.49% to 1.70% of articles, coinciding with the global GPR index spike to 330.18.
The March 2026 China GPR spike of 1.70% exceeded the previous 2022 peak of 2.47% in relative terms but represented the second-highest level since 2017.
China's geopolitical risk showed a declining trend from the May 2026 peak of 1.73% to October 2026 at 0.84%, representing a 51% reduction over five months.

The historical China GPR series (gprhc_chn) reached 1.57% in March 2026, the highest level in the 10-year lookback period, indicating elevated risk even when measured against longer-term historical newspapers.
China's October 2026 GPR level of 0.84% remained elevated compared to the 2024 second-half average of approximately 0.75%, suggesting persistent above-baseline geopolitical tensions.

summary: China experienced a severe geopolitical risk escalation in early 2026, with the GPR index reaching historic peaks in March 2026 at 1.70% of newspaper articles, the highest level in the recent 10-year data series [geopolitical:CHN:001][geopolitical:CHN:004]. This spike was part of a sharp surge from January to March 2026, coinciding with a global GPR index spike to 330.18 [geopolitical:CHN:004]. Risk remained elevated through May 2026 at 1.73%, sustaining levels more than double the 2019-2021 baseline [geopolitical:CHN:002]. While the March 2026 peak was lower than the March 2022 spike of 2.47%, it represented the second-highest level since 2017 [geopolitical:CHN:005]. The historical GPR series also confirmed elevated risk, reaching 1.57% in March 2026 [geopolitical:CHN:007]. Since the spring peak, China's geopolitical risk has declined significantly, falling 51% from May to October 2026 [geopolitical:CHN:006]. As of October 2026, the index stood at 0.84%, down from peak levels but still above the 2020-2021 baseline and the 2024 second-half average [geopolitical:CHN:003][geopolitical:CHN:008].
